sentences: A woman holds a small child firmly on her lap and washes the child's foot in the basin below.
Mary Cassatt, an American painter who worked in Paris, painted this scene in 1893, and such moments of physical closeness between a woman and a child were her signature subject.
The steep view from above makes the space shallow, so the carpeted floor seems to stand upright on the surface of the canvas.
Pattern fills the picture, from clothing to floor, adding to that flatness and reflecting Cassatt's intense engagement with Japanese art in the 1890s.
In the lower left, on the floor, she signed her name, 'Mary Cassatt', in blue paint.
The painting was first shown at her exhibition at the Galeries Durand-Ruel in Paris in 1893 and was widely exhibited after that; the Art Institute of Chicago bought it in 1910.
After Cassatt died in 1926, the museum hung it again that December in a memorial exhibition of her work.
